item.title: The Spire - needs greenlights
item.content:encoded:
It's a chemically changing rock. Name is work in progress, and I'm not too happy with the discovery, so any help/suggestions would be nice

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror/intriguing?

Page Layout (Optional): Standard article. After description, will go over discovery, and after discovery will then go over test logs.

Elevator Pitch: It's a tall rock that slightly twists. The tip of it will be called element A, and the base of it will be called element B. If an object touches the tip, element A changes into the majority of the atoms in that object. There are various things that cause a teleport event, but when that happens, the spire disappears and reappears at a random spot on the earth. element B then becomes the old element A, element A becomes the closest solid element near the tip, and the spire absorbs every current element B atom in a 1km radius.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: It was discovered when a redacted reality bender started rampaging, and along with various other items it created the spire. Some clean up MTF member accidentally touches the tip with his glove, and his glove disappears along with the spire. It's found in some town where around half of the people there dropped dead and withered on the spot, because the glove was mostly carbon, and all the carbon was stolen from their bodies. The spire is found in the town, and it's got a carbon base with a solid oxygen tip (from the oxygen in the granite that built the town)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The rules for the spire are pretty strict, so it's like a constant reminder that whatever the old tip was, all those atoms could immediately disappear in the center of a city, but it could also appear in the center of a forest, and be difficult to track down, so I feel that would draw people into the story. Also there's a mention near the beginning about testing being discontinued, so I feel people would want to see why

Additional Notes: The things that cause a teleportation event(work in progress name) are: The tip is touched with the same majority atom as the tip already had, so instead of staying the same it teleports. 108 hours pass without a tip change. If the tip is a radioactive element, the moment an atom in it decays, it undergoes the event (which is pretty much instantly). If the tip and base are the same element, it undergoes the event. If the tip is helium, it undergoes the event. I can explain more, as a lot of the info had to be cut down due to size limit.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: HOT SIRENS IN YOUR AREA - Greenlights needed!
item.description: A coven of sirens- yes, like the mythological Greek kind-
item.content:encoded:
A coven of sirens- yes, like the mythological Greek kind- find themselves adapting to the modern climate in order to seek their prey.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: Comedy, mainly, but not in an un-serious manner.

Elevator Pitch: You know those clearly fake ads you get on nsfw websites? The ones that’re like “HOT SINGLES IN YOUR AREA”, et cetera. Yeah. Those, but anomalous, and set up by Sirens, as in the type that’d lure sailors to death. The ad, if loaded on a page, would display a message along the lines of “10 HOT (xyz) WITHIN (distance)! TEXT NOW!”

+ show block
– hide block

As time went by, the distance would gradually decrease, and the number increase. This would culminate in the subject being ambushed, and then… well, consumed, by a number of horrible, vaguely humanoid fishy-people.

The Foundation would later track these ads to a certain location, and, unable to block the ads via webcrawlers or other non-anomalous means, would send in an MTF team to find out what’s going on. There’s an exploration log, and the anomaly is accidentally neutralised when the coven of sirens panics upon realising there’s angry fellows with guns in the hideout and collapses the building in order to escape, breaking all of their paratech that let them make and maintain the anomalous ads in the first place.

Central Narrative: The context behind this strange new manner of Greek monsters luring in prey is simply that people don’t usually fall for the ole’ “Sing to the sailors until they follow you and drown” trick, and they’ve had to resort to new and unusual means of tracking targets. Inkeeping with the tradition of luring sailors in with beautiful songs and false faces, they decide to essentially hijack NSFW spam ads, which ends up working pretty well.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As far as I’m aware, nobody’s done sirens as an SCP before, and beyond that, the concept of the fake ads on the sides of sketchy sites actually being dangerous beyond just giving your computer malware is a little spine-chilling. And also really funny, when you think about it.

Additional Notes: As this would be my first SCP, essentially any critique at all would be greatly appreciated.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts and properly space your paragraphs. ~Zyn

item.title: Sentient, climate-conscious tree
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Dunno

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: A tree that is intelligent and sentient and has an effect on kids and teens that come into direct contact with it that causes them to be protective of it and environmentally conscious. A small number of these young people are able to communicate with it by writing on its branches or trunk and receiving a reply written in moss that only they can interpret. It caused a month long strike by these affected youths that the foundation struggled to break up.

Central Narrative: The tree became anomalous in the late 1800s when the industrial revolution was pumping out pollution. It became more active in the past few decades after it was told by affected kids about climate change and deforestation and so on. The tree is pretty angry and upset at all this so when someone decides to cut it down to build on the land, the tree goes into full rage mode and for four straight weeks all affected kids surrounded the tree and refused to move, not even to eat or sleep though they had no symptoms of death from this. The tree eventually chills out after the foundation uses one of kids as a messenger to talk with it and promise (on behalf of the foundation) to look after it.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Poor tree doesn’t want to die. Makes sure everyone knows it.

Additional Notes: Criticise away!

item.title: "When We Didn't Dream" - An SCP Tale Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
A troublesome teenager utilizes mysterious livestock to control his dreams. A tale about SCP-1498.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: Tale

This tale doesn't take place in The Foundation itself. It's based around one specific SCP before it was contained.

Elevator Pitch: A teenager by the name of Ty encounters SCP-1498 in the woods, and begins to abuse its abilities. However, when he slowly starts to become an instance of SCP-1498, he struggles to find help. This takes place a month before SCP-1498's original containment date.

Central Narrative: Taking place in august of 1965, just before SCP-1498 (which this tale is about) is contained, a troublesome teenager, Ty, stumbles across SCP-1498 in the woods and learns that he can order dreams from the SCP. He begins to abuse the ability, spending most of his time asleep, dreaming. However, when his body begins to slowly turn into instances of the SCP, he attempts to find "The Oneiroi Collective" (the people who possibly designed the SCP) to help him. However, upon searching phone books, he discovers that the phone number to call them only exists on the instances of SCP-1498. He hurries back to where he last saw them, but they've vanished completely. Luckily, a phone wire that goes through the woods leads him to an abandoned office building, where he finds the livestock entering. Ty catches up to them, managing to get on the phone with The Oneiroi Collective. However, it's too late, and Ty completely transforms into an instance of SCP-1498-1, mindlessly wandering back into the woods, ironically dreaming of the days when he didn't dream at all.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The realization that Ty basically has no way out of the situation he's in. This is the foundation of most of the tension throughout the tale, as it will seem almost completely hopeless. Which, by the end, it's revealed that it was, indeed, hopeless. At least, that's the goal I'll try to achieve with this tale.

Additional Notes: Obviously, this is a rough outline of what happens, and it will almost certainly change (hopefully for the better) if this gets greenlighted. I'm also not the author of SCP-1498, and as so tried to keep this story as distant from the lore set up in the SCP itself.

Here's a link to SCP-1498, which this tale is based on: http://www.scpwiki.com/scp-1498

item.title: Television POV(Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Mystery

Page Layout: Standard SCP article.

Elevator Pitch: SCP is a 4k HDTV with a standard TV remote. When you switch the input to HDMI-1 you can see a POV of a random person in the world. Changing the channel would change the POV to another random individual.

Central Narrative: The article would explore several unique circumstances, like a POV of someone dying, someone who needs glasses, someone tripping on hallucinogens, someone dreaming, someone with color-blindness, etcetera.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The chances of you finding your own POV out of 7 billion people would be virtually impossible. So I'd describe a process where SCP scientists use several d-class's to keep flipping through channels until they come across somebody who worked for the SCP foundation. They'd be found and then asked to stare in front of the TV. What happens is essentially they'd be staring at an infinite mirror, the user of this circumstance would enter into a trance and would require a third party to get them away from the TV. The person in question would eventually wake up and explain what exactly they felt.

Additional Notes: What kind of feelings would they experience? Nirvana? Dread? Would they want to immediately kill themselves? I know that's kind of played out but I want to make sure I hit all the beats.

item.title: concept idea!
item.description: Just looking for advice or comments on this idea for an SCP
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action/History

Page Layout (Optional): Basic format containment then background of SCP

Elevator Pitch: An SCP item that gives the wearer invincibility inhumane strength and expansive knowledge of combat and war strategy. It comes in the form of a suit of spartan armor that will transform into whatever armor the wearer knows of.

Central Narrative: The armor was discovered during the Vietnam war and captured by the Foundation they then found through testing and a few containment incidents the basic abilities of the armor as well as learning with untrained individuals it will cause them to enter a blood rage upon putting it on and it will deteriorate their body killing them within hours of exposure. With individuals trained extensively in combat the blood rage will not take hold unless under extreme emotional or physical stress and the armor will deteriorate much slowly causing death much later (possibly years) than other subjects. The armor is permitted to be used in world ending situations and large site containment breaches. The armor also has access to famous warrior throughout history and the deterioration seen in subjects is most likely due to this effect as the armor will steal and contain your spirit. It also has a calling effect that pulls nearby personnel into attempting to wear it resulting in their deaths. The armor was originally created during the Battle of Thermopylae when a Persian soldier donned the armor of Leonidas causing his spirit to put a curse on the armor (causing the effects seen today).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP is a tool the Foundation can use to combat many of the threats the Foundation faces however it is a very unstable tool and finding a suitable subject is incredibly difficult as most will die within hours, also it creates an effect similar to the "One Ring" from Lord of the Rings in which it pulls people towards it and typically has them fight over the owner of the armor which is very dangerous as many valuable Foundation assets could be drawn to it and die to the wearer. Also the amount of knowledge the armor holds from its past users could prove useful to the Foundation as well as its extensive knowledge of strategy.

Additional Notes: I feel as if I am missing something to make this story truly unique and I hope someone can take notes on this and help me figure out how to properly narrow down my ideas or give it an extra hook of some sort.

item.title: Memetic Instruction Pamphlets
item.description: Anomalous instruction pamphlets designed to maim/kill
item.content:encoded:
Anomalous instruction pamphlets designed to maim/kill seemingly random people across the globe… (all criticism welcome)

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mystery

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous set of pamphlets that compel the reader to do whatever the pamphlet has written on it- for example, if one said "read this pamphlet over and over", the subject would be forced to read the pamphlet over and over until it is taken from them or they expire.

Central Narrative: A group of researchers testing the capabilities of the SCP after MTF recovery units with memetic resistance find multiple pamphlets in seemingly random homes in urban areas such as Berlin, NYC, and London. Interviews with the owners of the homes show that they all have had attempts on their lives through anomalous means within the past three months.

+ show block
– hide block

The people are administered amnestics and are put back in their homes with a Foundation agent trailing them to make sure they are not killed. The researchers begin investigations on possible reasons why the makers of the pamphlets are targeting these people. One of the D-Class testing personnel notices that the contents of the pamphlet have changed.

The pamphlet writes about how the hitmen attempting to kill these people know that the Foundation has acquired the pamphlets and that the hitmen will not be so careless in the future, potentially setting up an opportunity for there to be more to the story.

The Foundation intercepts a radio transmission detailing the failure of the pamphlets, and discussing potential plans for the future. Foundation agents find a connection between the targets of the killings: they have all been involved in numerous black-market purchases of anomalous objects.

The Foundation discovers the existence of a group of assassins hired by existing groups to carry out their dirty work. The group has been implicated in over 260 murders, burglaries and other crimes across the globe, starting in 2008.

The article ends with all the pamphlets changing to contain the message WE’LL BE WATCHING. SIGNED WITH LOVE, THE SWORD OF THE KING

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The different pamphlets have different instructions tailored to the individuals who received them. Each of them seems to be designed to seriously maim or kill the person who received them. The mystery of why these people are being targeted by anomalous killers is also a good hook.

Additional Notes: With this SCP, I am hoping to set up an opportunity for a new GOI or POI and more SCPs. All criticism is appreciated!

item.title: Te Horoi Pai (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: Second SCP proposal based on a revisited concept.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Mystery

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch: A tube of Petroleum jelly. When ointment is applied to a human, a person's hygiene is enhanced. Prominent symptom manifest in the form of pheromone secretion and irrational compulsion to spread the ointment. Hours after patient zero is infected, the infected encounter amorphous entities. Appearing entities embody subconscious fetishes or extremest fears. They ignore beings lacking pheromone and are hostile to those marked with pheromone.

Central Narrative: On the 9th December, the mysterious disappearance of 25 guests and staff at the Westhaven Luxury Lodge made national headlines. A team of four Field Agents stationed at Nelson, New Zealand take over the investigation and create a cover story.

Field Agents are briefed about the crime scene by the police. Exploring the lodge they find five rooms in the hallway cordoned off by police tape. Foundation agents are alarmed by the crude messages scratched into the Manuka wood and signs glued onto the walls left behind by the lodging's former occupants. Text advertise and revere "a conditioner sent by the gods". Most jarringly, the other remainder of the text read "The knavish resistance were enlightened, now they too relish the heaven-sent scent". Conditioner called "Te Horoi Pai" , translated to Xtreme Conditioner is discovered and placed in containment. All other copies found in the Lodging or within Police custody are confiscated and destroyed.

Testing is conducted, discovering the anomaly's psycho-contagious nature. It's speculated an unknown G.O.I is at hand. A nationwide sweep, extensively covering every hotel, motel and supermarket in New Zealand, yields negative results. A Mobile Taskforce (Called Bad Hair Day) is conceived to monitor the domestic supply chain for wild instances.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Mass disappearance is unheard-of in the 21st century, creating mystery. The anomaly takes place in New Zealand. Testing reveals the ultimate fate of the Lodging's residents. Furthermore, the G.O.I theory is a hypothesis, since Te Horoi Pai is the product name but there is no brand associated nor a manufacturer stated on the bottle. Therefore, the Foundation attempts to contain a contagious SCP with no identified point of origin; an analogy for viral outbreak clusters with no immediate causes.

Additional Notes: This is a submission for my first "canon" SCP, so any form of criticism is appreciated (Bluntness is 100% tolerated but please be constructive).

item.title: The Perpetual Lawnmower
item.description: A lawnmower that perpetually gets faster, till exposed to grass.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlight.
SCP Article.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a lawnmower that perpetually gets faster and doesn't suffer from wind resistance or interact with physical objects, until it comes into contact with grass. When it touches grass it becomes 'real' and suffers the effects of wind resistance from the speed that it is going.

Central Narrative: This is an anomaly created by a new POI, who created this specifically to mow their lawn for them without any effort. In interviews conducted by foundation personnel, it was revealed that the increasing speed was designed as a defense mechanism in the event that someone attempted to steal it for their own personal use. (Testing logs included in the article)

This SCP was found moving away from this POI's place of residence at very high speeds, allowing the foundation to get a rough idea to where this POI lives.

Hook: Its a dangerous lawnmower that was created by a dangerous POI with a sick sense of humor and karma.
